entries.note: PMID 9856949, Science 1998-12-01; quote verbatim in abstract. Opener. Note this system's own statement: IL-13 acts independently of eosinophils (matters for entry 5).
PMID 17898169, PNAS epub 2007-09-26; quote verbatim in abstract. Patient-derived ex-vivo track with its own model_id is right under decision 8.
PMID 21895629 (open access); quote verbatim. FDA 761180 integrated review lists the cynomolgus antigen-challenge study CAT354Rp038 (BAL eosinophil influx inhibited), so model_filed true holds.

PMID 22616628; quote verbatim (abstract). `same` holds only as a downstream readout (decision 15): FeNO is not the model's signature. Hanania 2015 Fig 3 tracks serum periostin itself under lebrikizumab; cite it. prediction_level should be class; PubMed record created 2012-05, so decision 7 likely dates it 2012.

PMID 29793857, registry 2019-01-08 confirmed. Two systems share one model_id: the contradicted eosinophil prediction is May 2012's IL-13-humanised OVA mouse (tralokinumab dosed), not Wills-Karp's WT OVA mouse, which stated eosinophil-independence. Give the humanised mouse its own track (contra there); WT track untested (#90, split literature, AHR/mucus never measured).
entries.adjudication_note: Decision 8: May 2012's IL-13-humanised OVA mouse (tralokinumab's own model) is a separate track from Wills-Karp's wild-type mouse, which predicted eosinophil-independence (decision 4: its own prediction did not fail). AHR/mucus never measured: untested; open the humanised track contra 2018.

entries.note: Same source; FDA 761180 confirms the monkey model (CAT354Rp038) predicted inhibited BAL eosinophil influx; MESOS: blood eosinophil ratio 1.21 (p=0.055), sputum 0.57 (p=0.63), FeNO 0.78 (p=0.023). Product in both model and trial; contra stands.
May 2012 abstract states affinity and in-vivo efficacy, no exposure target or margin; untested is right (decision 16: no stated margin).

PMID 29792288, epub 2018-05-20; registry 2018-03-21 (STRATOS 2) / 2018-04-17 (STRATOS 1) confirmed. Case 3 (reached, failed, abandoned) → contra derived_from efficacy. FDA 2022 review: monkey NOAEL 90 (26-wk) and 100 (13-wk) mg/kg/week, first public 2022, so margin_stated null is right; see rule question 5.
Wills-Karp 1998 abstract, verbatim. Opener on the WT OVA mouse track.
Woodruff 2007 abstract, verbatim. Patient-level track opener.
PMID 21812663, NEJM epub 2011-08-03; primary FEV1 met (+5.5 points, p=0.02). NCT00930163 has no posted results (confirmed). same + direction_only is right.

Same source; prespecified periostin split 8.2 vs 1.6 points, verbatim. comparison_stated true is generous (the trial states the hypothesis and the split, not the model data); status unchanged either way.
May 2012 abstract, verbatim; CAT354Rp038 in the FDA review confirms model_filed. Separate primate track is right.

PMID 22743678 (open access), epub 2012-06-27, registry 2017-02-23 confirmed. ACQ-6 primary missed; FEV1 secondary 0.21 vs 0.06 L, p=0.072, not significant, so #32 does not apply. model_src here is May 2012 (humanised mouse) while entries 3 and 9 cite Wills-Karp: same decision-8 split as engagement 5; contra holds on either track.
Same source and trial on the monkey track; primary (ACQ-6) missed, secondary not significant; contra under the primary-endpoint rule.

PMID 23726041, epub 2013-05-29; NCT00971035 no posted results (confirmed). FEV1 primary missed with no periostin split: a direct failure of the patient-level prediction; the treatment-failure secondary moved regardless of periostin, so #32 does not rescue.

PMID 24582316, epub 2014-02-28, registry 2017-12-12 confirmed. No significant secondary; a clean second miss, strengthens is right. NCT01130064 (dectrekumab) confirmed completed 2012-04 with no results.

PMID 26231288, registry 2017-03-06 confirmed. Primary missed but FEV1 secondary significant (+7.3%, 95% CI 2.6-12.0, p=0.003) and the source does not call it a match: #32 makes this untested, not a strengthening miss. Track stays contra from 2012; TROPOS/STRATOS carry the later misses.
entries.adjudication_note: Decision 4 (#32): primary missed, FEV1 secondary significant, and Brightling 2015 does not call it a match, so untested, not a strengthening miss (decision 7). Cyno track stays contra from 2012; this trial belongs in patient_trials.

entries.note: PMID 27616196, epub 2016-09-05; NCT01867125 results 2026-07-17, NCT01868061 none, confirmed. LAVOLTA I met its biomarker-high primary at both doses, LAVOLTA II missed (RR 0.74, p=0.06); drafter's own source_calls_it is unresolved, which #90 scores untested. Track stays contra from 2013.
entries.adjudication_note: Decision 4 (#90): the drafter's own source_calls_it is unresolved and LAVOLTA II's effect was present (RR 0.74), not absent, so neither contra nor same; decision 11's partial covers readouts within one source, not replicate trials. Track stays contra from 2013.

entries.note: PMID 29792288; both primaries missed (all-comers RR 0.93; FeNO-high RR 0.84) and the source calls the mechanism failed; no FEV1 secondary seen in the abstract, so #32 not applied. Add TROPOS (NCT02281357) to patient_trials.

May 2012 abstract, verbatim; proxy opener. FDA 761180 confirms 13-week and 26-week cynomolgus studies; FDA 761306 (lebrikizumab) line 1759: NOAEL was the highest dose tested in all three monkey studies, so the pooled model label holds.

Quote verbatim at 761180 integrated review p.116 (NOAEL 90 mg/kg/week). Same document: AD conjunctivitis 7.4% vs 3.0% and monkey ophthalmoscopy 'no treatment related changes', an askable silence. Decision 12 transfers cross-indication harms symmetrically; the draft imported the clean reconciliation but not the harm. Asthma pools show no excess; see rule question 3.
entries.adjudication_note: RULE QUESTION: decision 12 imports cross-indication harms symmetrically but does not rank an import against in-context patient data. Over 4,000 asthma patients show no conjunctivitis excess: does the in-context null govern, or does AD conjunctivitis score contra with imported_from?

entries.note: PMID 21895629 abstract, verbatim. PubMed/entrez 2011-09-08, print May 2012: 2011 under decision 7 (the cyno-track entries on the same paper carry 2012, a tile-level inconsistency). Own track as adjudicated at engagement 5.

PMID 29793857 abstract verbatim; NCT02449473 results 2019-01-08 confirmed. Model predicted BAL eosinophilia inhibited; MESOS bronchial 1.43, sputum 0.57, blood 1.21 unchanged: contra, the humanised-track opening the engagement-5 adjudication asked for. Downstream tier right.

PMID 27885827 (PMC5192997) verbatim; PubMed 2016-11-26. Full text: calibrated on in-vitro and baseline eosinophil data, verified against published drug-response data (Corren, Hanania, Piper), so the opener is a formality before the retro entry.

Verbatim. Full text: model 'calibrated and verified using separate sets of published clinical data', the phase 2 blood-eosinophil rises it reproduces; built 2016 after them, so retro never same (decision 10). retrodiction true right.

Same MESOS abstract. The airway eosinophil fall was the model's one untested 2016 prediction; MESOS primary (bronchial biopsy) 1.43, sputum 0.57: failed. Blood 1.21 (p=0.055) is not a matched pre-specified readout, so decision 11 partial does not rescue; contra.
PMID 28758192 verbatim; epub 2017-09-28 (PubMed 2017-08-02). Built for phase 3 dose selection before STRATOS started (2014-06), so prospective, not post-hoc; no margin stated, untested opener right.

PMID 29792288 verbatim; registry 2018-03-21/04-17 confirmed. Case 3 (reached, failed, abandoned) gives the derived contra. NCT02161757 results: the model's own readout moved at 300 mg q2w (pre-BD FEV1 week 52 +6.03%, 95% CI 2.34-9.73); see rule question.
May 2012 abstract verbatim; 2011 per decision 7 (entrez 2011-09-08). Opener on the only mouse the product was dosed in, split from the WT OVA track as adjudicated.
PMID 22743678 verbatim; epub 2012-06-27, registry 2017-02-23. ACQ-6 primary missed, FEV1 secondary p=0.072 n.s., so #32 not triggered; contra matches the efficacy 6/7 verdicts on the sibling tracks.

PMID 29792288 verbatim; STRATOS 1/2 primaries missed, TROPOS OCS primary missed (p=0.271, NCT02281357 results 2018-05-16); source calls the IL-13 role unsupported. Strengthens right; Brightling 2015 in patient_trials only, consistent with the efficacy-10 adjudication.

NCT00781443 resolves (start 2008-12, n=29, no results); title verbatim. A results-free registry record is a sponsor statement, not a source (#125). Open on Scheerens 2014 (PMID 24131304, tier 1, online 2013-10-18) at 2013; keep model_first_use_year 2008; before the same-year contra (#30).

Noonan verbatim (epub 2013-05-29); Scheerens online 2013-10-18, so 2013. Challenge ran 2008-12 to 2009-11, before MOLLY finished (2010-12): prospective, not retro. Source calls the n.s. 48% a reduction (#10 mirror); Noonan is the model's own no-ICS population, MILLY's is not. Contra holds; see rule questions.

PMID 29413502 verbatim; epub 2017-12-13, NCT02104674 results 2026-07-17 confirmed. Primary missed (83 mL, p=0.06), no significant secondary, authors call it a miss; challenge public since 2013, so cleanly prospective. Strengthens right.

missing: Lebrikizumab whole-lung allergen challenge (Scheerens 2014, PMID 24131304, doi:10.1111/cea.12220; NCT00781443, n=29, no results posted): a human_challenge model with a member drug, primary LAR reduced 48% but not significant (95% CI -19 to 90), larger in periostin/IgE/eosinophil-high subjects. Decision 8 puts allergen challenge in scope; the draft cites the paper only for CCL13/CCL17 and gives it no track.

TROPOS (NCT02281357, phase 3 OCS-sparing, registry results 2018-05-16; Busse 2019 Eur Respir J, PMID 30442714, doi:10.1183/13993003.00948-2018): primary missed (OCS reduction 37.6% vs 29.9%, p=0.271) with no secondary met. A member phase 3 failure absent from the draft and from the STRATOS entry's patient_trials.

Korenblat 2018 (Respir Med, PMID 29413502, doi:10.1016/j.rmed.2017.12.006, epub 2017-12-13): second lebrikizumab trial in ICS-free mild-to-moderate asthma, FEV1 primary missed (83 mL, p=0.06), 'inhibiting IL-13 in this population was not sufficient to improve lung function'. Replicates Noonan 2013 on the hbe-il13-signature and WT-mouse tracks; absent.

IL-13-humanised OVA mouse dosed with tralokinumab (May 2012, doi:10.1111/j.1476-5381.2011.01659.x; FDA 761180 nonclinical pharmacology): the only mouse the product itself was dosed in and a genetically distinct system from Wills-Karp's WT OVA mouse; it needs its own model_id (decision 8) rather than sharing ova-mouse-il13.

Out of class, for the record: Gauvreau 2011 (PMID 21057005, doi:10.1164/rccm.201008-1210OC) IMA-638/IMA-026 allergen challenge is the class's human-challenge precedent, but anrukinzumab is not a listed member, so it is not scorable.
could_not_verify: Panettieri 2018 FEV1 secondary significance (not in the abstract; full text paywalled).
Lebrikizumab adolescent phase 3 (ACOUSTICS) outcome: wrong NCT retrieved on first try, not pursued within budget.
Hanania 2015 Fig 3 direction of the serum-periostin change (figure not readable from the XML text).
rule_questions: Decision 4 #32 names only the match-call rescue: when a trial misses its primary, a lung-function secondary is significant, and the source's own conclusion calls the mechanism failed (Brightling 2015; possibly STRATOS), is the entry untested (literal #32) or contra?

Replicate phase 3s in the model-selected population with one primary met and one missed (LAVOLTA I/II, biomarker-high): same + source_calls_it partial, untested (#90 unresolved), or contra on the patient-level track?

Decision 12 transfers cross-indication safety comparisons symmetrically. When the imported harm (AD conjunctivitis, monkey ophthalmoscopy clean) is directly contradicted by the context's own trials (>4,000 asthma patients, no excess), does the in-context null govern, or does the import still score contra with imported_from?

Is a humanised-target knock-in mouse (IL-13-humanised OVA mouse, May 2012) the same track as the wild-type model of the same challenge (Wills-Karp 1998) when the two systems' stated predictions on a readout (eosinophils) differ?

Decision 16 on a track whose floor is a derived contra: the cynomolgus NOAEL (90-100 mg/kg/week) held in patients but became public only in the 2022 FDA review, after the class failed. Is a 2022 ceiling entry (same, margin_stated true) written, and does it change the track's dose status?

Engagement readout substitution: when the model's own readout (serum periostin) has a patient-side source but the drafter scored a different downstream readout (FeNO) as same, does the track carry same, or must the entry cite the model's readout (decision 4 'the PD readout the model used')?

[models] A human-challenge model whose own primary missed significance (LAR -48%, 95% CI -19 to 90, n=29) but whose source calls it a reduction: is the source's call a stated positive prediction (mirror of #10), or is a non-significant model primary no prediction, leaving the track untested?

[models] One drug, two populations on one track: does a contra in the population the model tested (no ICS; Noonan 2013, Korenblat 2018) outrank the same drug's same in a population the model never tested (ICS-treated MILLY)? Decision 6 (#3) ranks only across drugs.

[models] Dose case 3 when the model's own readout was met: the tralokinumab PK/PD model predicted near-maximal FEV1 at 300 mg q2w and STRATOS 1 pre-BD FEV1 rose 6.03% (95% CI 2.34-9.73) at that regimen while AAER failed. Derived contra (decision 4) or a decision-9 surrogate-matched same with outcome_tested negative?
